Discussion of the words of Allah, the Exalted:

[4–6] ﴿Do they not think that they will be resurrected﴾ ﴿for a tremendous Day﴾ ﴿the Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds﴾.

Then He, glorified is He, said, threatening them: ﴿Do they not think that they will be resurrected﴾, i.e., from their graves after their death.

﴿For a tremendous Day﴾, i.e., one of great terror, of grave matter, of abundant dread. Whoever loses on it will be made to enter a scorching fire.

﴿The Day when mankind will stand﴾, i.e., before His command and His judgment concerning them, to receive what they deserve, in a standing place where the criminal is overwhelmed by such terror that he would wish to ransom himself with everything he could.

In the fact that the Woe (al-Wayl) is applied to those who give short measure (al-Mutaffifin) with what is mentioned in these two verses, there are intensifications in forbidding short-measuring and magnifying its sin. The reason for this, as al-Shihab (al-Khafaji) summarized it, is that mentioning "thinking" (al-zann) together with the demonstrative (ism al-ishara), which indicates distance, implies ignorance and contempt; and describing the Day of their standing as "great" and substituting "the Day when mankind will stand" for it indicates the magnifying of what they had held in contempt.

Wisdom requires that not even the weight of an atom's worth of good or evil be neglected.

The title (Lord of the worlds) denotes the Owner and the Nurturer, indicating that no mighty wrongdoer escapes Him, and He does not leave the right of a weak oppressed person unfulfilled. In the magnifying of the matter of short-measuring there is an allusion to justice and its balance, and that one who does not neglect the like of this, how could He neglect the suspension of the law of His justice among His servants? And it is sufficient that He described them with the attributes of disbelievers. So reflect on this station, for in it is what imaginations are bewildered by.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[14] ﴿Nay! Rather, what they used to earn has covered over their hearts.﴾

﴿Nay﴾ means: these verses are not "tales of the ancients." Rather, they are the manifest truth and a healing for what is in the breasts. ﴿Rather, what they used to earn has covered over their hearts﴾ means: what they acquired of sins has veiled their perceptive faculties, until it clouded their essence and became a rust upon it through its becoming firmly fixed. The *rayn* (a stain or rust that settles and does not come off, here meaning the heart's covering by sin) is a term whose root meaning is rust and a settled filth. Love of sins that becomes firmly rooted in the soul is likened to it, because repeated action produces a firm disposition that does not cease, and a quality that remains lodged in the soul. Thus through the abundance of sins, love of them becomes entrenched in the heart in such a way that it does not depart, like rust that does not easily come off.

In *al-Asas* it is said: *al-rayn* is what covers the heart and mounts upon it of hardness toward sin after sin, from their saying: "The drink and the drowsiness covered him (*raana 'alayhi*)," and: "He was overcome by it (*raana bihi*)," when it overpowers his intellect; and: "He was covered by (*rīna bi-fulān*)." Its counterpart is *al-ghayn*.

The discussion on the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, exalted is He:

[15] ﴿Nay! Indeed they, on that Day, will be veiled from their Lord.﴾

﴿Nay﴾ is a rebuke to them for the earning that has covered their hearts, or it means "truly." ﴿Indeed they, on that Day, will be veiled from their Lord.﴾ Ibn Jarir said: That is, they will not see Him, and none of His honor will reach them. So they are veiled from seeing Him and from His honor. Singling out these people for veiling implies that others are not veiled, so Allah will see them and they will see His honor. Al-Shihab said: Since the hijab (veil) is that which screens with a curtain of silk or other material, it was used figuratively (istiʿara) at one time for not seeing, because the veiled person does not see what is veiled, and at another time for humiliation, because the lowly is veiled and prevented from entering upon the great. Therefore the Arabs said: "People are between one who is welcomed and one who is veiled," meaning: one who is honored and one who is humiliated. In these meanings it is impossible for Allah to be described by it, so it is not valid to apply it to Him, exalted is He, as the scholars have explicitly stated. It is only used to describe creatures, as in this verse. When it is applied to one of His names, exalted is He, it is an attribute by way of cause (sababi) and not a literal one. Rather, it is a likening to creation.

(p-6097)

The discussion of the words of His Exalted Saying:

[16–17] ﴿Then indeed they will be burning in Hellfire.﴾ ﴿Then it will be said, "This is what you used to deny."﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 17]

﴿Then indeed they will be burning in Hellfire﴾: that is, they will be burning in it. Al-Qashani (Qashani) has pointed to the secret of the sequence of these noble sentences, namely that the sins they acquired, once they became like rust upon their hearts through becoming firmly rooted in them, clouded their essence and changed it from its natural disposition. At that point the veil was established and the door of forgiveness was closed. Therefore He said:

﴿No! Indeed, they will be veiled from their Lord that Day﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 15], because their hearts are unable to receive the light, and it is impossible for them to return to their original natural purity. This is like sulphurous water, for example: if it is filtered or distilled, it does not return to its cool watery nature, because its substance has been transformed. This is unlike heated water, whose quality has changed while its nature remains. For this reason they deserve eternal abiding in the punishment. They were judged by His saying: ﴿Then indeed they will be burning in Hellfire.﴾ End of quotation.

Ibn al-Qayyim said in (Bada'i' al-Fawa'id) regarding this verse, in substance: God, glorified is He, combined for them two punishments: the punishment of the veil and the punishment of the Fire. The pain of the veil works upon their hearts and spirits the same effect that the fire works upon their bodies, like the state of one who is prevented from the thing he loves most in this world and is seized by the severest punishment. For the most specific punishment of the spirit is that it becomes attached to a beloved on whom it cannot do without, while it is prevented from reaching him. How much more so if, along with the beloved's remoteness from it and the length of his concealment, there is added his hatred for it, his aversion, his rejection, and his fierce anger against it? Then what proportion does bodily pain bear to this pain, which none can conceive except one who has been afflicted with it or with some part of it? If souls were to imagine the pain and anguish of God, glorified is He, veiling Himself from them on the Day of meeting Him, they would not expose themselves to the causes of that veiling. And you see lovers in this world, for a form whose ultimate beauty is only known to them, how they cry out from the pain of their beloved's veiling himself from them, his turning away and his abandonment. One of them sees separation as death or worse than death, from a single moment, as he said:

I used to regard separation for a single night as death, so how then with a separation whose appointed time is the Gathering?

(p-6098) The state of this is only made clear by knowing what the spirit was created for, what it was prepared for, and what it was fashioned upon, and that there is no happiness, bliss, or life for it except by attaining it.

Know that God, glorified is He, created each of the limbs for a purpose and a benefit, so its perfection and pleasure lie in its attaining what it was created for. He created the eye for seeing, the ear for hearing, the nose for smelling, the tongue for speech, the hand for grasping, and the foot for walking, and He created the spirit for knowing Him, loving Him, delighting in His nearness, and savouring His remembrance. He made this its perfection and its ultimate end. When it is deprived of this, it is in a worse state than the eye, the ear, the tongue, the hand, and the foot when they are deprived of what they were created for and are prevented from it. Indeed, there is absolutely no comparison between the pain of this spirit and the pain of those deprived limbs; rather, its pain is the greatest pain, and it is of the same kind as its pain when it loses the thing it loves most and holds most dear, is prevented from it, and sees others who have attained its union, won its nearness, and gained its pleasure. The spirit has no life, no bliss, no joy, and no delight except in God alone being its worshipped one, its god, and its aim, the one in whom its eye finds comfort only through His nearness, intimacy with Him, and devoting itself wholly to His love and longing for His meeting. This is the ultimate of its perfection, its greatest bliss, and its hastened paradise in this world. When the Day of His meeting comes, its greatest bliss will be the lifting of the veil (p-6099) that used to screen it in this world from seeing His Face and hearing His speech. In the hadith of the vision: "By God, He has given them nothing more beloved to them than gazing upon His Face."

Then he said: Just as He, glorified is He, combined for His enemies these two punishments, namely the pain of the veil and the pain of torment, so He combined for His lovers two kinds of bliss: the bliss of nearness and gazing, and the bliss of eating, drinking, marriage, and enjoying what is in Paradise, in His saying: ﴿And He will give them radiance and joy﴾ [al-Insan: 11], and the verses that follow.

﴿Then it will be said, "This is what you used to deny"﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 17]: that is, in the world. Al-Imam (al-Razi) said: as a rebuke to them and an increase in their humiliation, for indeed the most severe thing for a person, when some harm befalls him and he is in pain from it, is to be reminded that the means of deliverance from his affliction were before him and he neglected them, and the means of escape from it were within his reach and he overlooked them.

[18–21] ﴿Indeed, no! Indeed, the record of the righteous is in ʿIlliyyūn.﴾ ﴿And what can make you know what ʿIlliyyūn is?﴾ [al-Muṭaffifīn: 19] ﴿It is a written record,﴾ [al-Muṭaffifīn: 20] ﴿witnessed by those brought near [to Allah].﴾ [al-Muṭaffifīn: 21]

﴿Kallā﴾ is a rebuke against denial, or it means "truly" (ḥaqqan). ﴿Indeed, the record of the righteous is in ʿIlliyyūn.﴾ Al-Qashani said: That is, what is recorded of the forms of the deeds of the blessed and the states of their luminous souls and their virtuous dispositions is in ʿIlliyyūn. It is the opposite of Sijjīn in its height and the elevation of its rank, and it is the register of the deeds of the people of goodness.

As He said: ﴿And what can make you know what ʿIlliyyūn is?﴾ [al-Muṭaffifīn: 19] ﴿It is a written record﴾ [al-Muṭaffifīn: 20], that is, an exalted place (p-6100) in which are inscribed the forms of their deeds.

﴿Witnessed by those brought near [to Allah]﴾ [al-Muṭaffifīn: 21], that is, those brought near from the presence of the Lord of Majesty attend it, as in the verse ﴿in a seat of truth, in the presence of a Sovereign, Omnipotent﴾ [al-Qamar: 55].

And the ones brought near are the righteous themselves: He repeated their mention with a second description, as an honouring of them and an enumeration of their attributes. Or they are the angels, as a exaltation of them and a magnifying of their station.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[22–26] ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss﴾ ﴿on couches, observing.﴾ ﴿You will recognize in their faces the radiance of bliss.﴾ ﴿They will be given to drink of a sealed nectar﴾ ﴿whose seal is musk. And for that let the competitors compete.﴾

When He, the Exalted, magnified their record (kitab), He followed it with the magnification of their station, by His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss﴾, meaning in great and enduring bliss, which is their bliss in the Gardens.

﴿On couches, observing﴾, meaning on thrones (asirra) and reclining couches (muttaka'at), looking at what Allah has given them of honour and of the varied forms of bliss.

﴿You will recognize in their faces the radiance of bliss﴾, meaning its brightness (bahja) and its sheen (raunaq), just as the sheen and beauty of those living in luxury are seen on their faces.

﴿They will be given to drink of a sealed nectar﴾, meaning of wine (khamr). However, it is specified as the pure kind that has no adulteration in it, as Hassan said:

They give to drink those who come to al-Barīṣ from them,
From Barada that flows with the pure, unmixed nectar.

From this is their saying: "Musk is nectar (rahiq), with no adulteration in it," and "Lineage is nectar, with no admixture in it."

And His saying, exalted is He:

﴿Sealed﴾, meaning He sealed its vessels as an honour to it, to protect it from being touched by hands, in accordance with the custom of sealing what is honoured and protected.

﴿Whose seal is musk﴾. Al-Qaffal said: That is, the thing with which the head of the flask of that nectar is sealed is musk, like the clay with which the mouths of flasks are sealed, so that this musk is moist and the seal imprints itself upon it.

It is related from some of the early scholars (salaf) and the lexicographers that "al-makhtum" is that which has a khitam, meaning an end (aqibah), and it has been explained as musk, meaning that whoever drinks it, the end of his drinking will be in the scent of musk. The intent is the pleasure of the final taste through the fragrance and its diffusion, unlike the wine of this world, which is foul in taste and smell.

﴿And for that﴾, meaning for the bliss mentioned and what follows it, ﴿let the competitors compete﴾, meaning let those who desire eagerly race to obedience to Allah, the Exalted.

Ibn Jarir said: Tanafus (competition) is that a man covets (yunaffis) something that another man has, and wishes that it be his instead of the other's. It is derived from "the precious thing" (nafis), which is what people's souls crave, seek and desire. It seems its meaning here is: let people strive diligently for it and toward it, and let them race to seek it, and let their souls be eager for it.

Al-Razi said: His, exalted is He, extreme exhortation toward it indicates the loftiness of its status. And there is in it an indication that competition should be for such great and enduring bliss, not for the bliss that is turbid and swiftly perishing. And His saying, exalted is He:

The discussion of His saying, the Exalted:

[27–28] ﴿And its mixture is from Tasnim﴾ ﴿a spring from which those brought near will drink﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 28]

﴿And its mixture is from Tasnim﴾ is conjoined to ﴿its seal is musk﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 26] as another attribute of ﴿sealed wine﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 25], and what lies between them is an interjected clause (i'tirad) that affirms its excellence. That is: what this sealed wine is mixed with is water of Tasnim. Tasnim, originally, is a verbal noun from sanamahu, meaning "he raised it," and from it comes al-sanam (the hump). The water was named after it because of its elevation and its pouring down from a height.

He clarified it by His saying ﴿a spring from which those brought near will drink﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 28], meaning: they drink the wine from it. There is a discussion regarding the particle bi (ba'), as in the verse ﴿a spring from which the servants of Allah will drink﴾ [al-Insan: 6], concerning whether it is superfluous (za'idah), or has the meaning of "min" (from), or is connected to the verb of mixing (al-imtizaj), or to the verb of delight (al-iltidhadh).

The discourse on the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[29–31] ﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed﴾ ﴿And when they passed by them, they would wink at one another﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 30] ﴿And when they returned to their families, they returned jesting﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 31]

﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes﴾ means the disbelievers of Quraysh. ﴿used to laugh at those who believed﴾ means they mocked them for their belief in Allah alone and in what He revealed to His Messenger, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, and for their rejection of what their fathers had been upon.

The Imam said: "Those who committed crimes are the transgressing leaders, whose souls had been steeped in evil and whose ears had been deafened to hearing the call to truth. These used to laugh at those who believed. That is because when Allah showed mercy to this world by sending the Prophet ﷺ, the great men of the people and their notables were following the opinion of the masses and were in the misguidance of the common folk. The call to truth was faint; only his voice, peace be upon him, was raised with it, and then some of those near him would whisper it, and among the weak who answered his call were those whose desires had not obscured the path of truth from their hearts, so they confided it to those they hoped in, and they could not proclaim it openly to those they feared. It is the nature of the strong, who take pride in power and numbers, to laugh at whoever opposes them in their way and calls them to something other than what they know, even though that person is weaker than them in strength and fewer in number. Such was the condition of a group of Quraysh, such as Abu Jahl, al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, al-As ibn Wa'il and their partisans. And thus is the condition of their likes in every age, when innovations (bid'ah) become widespread, sects scatter, the path of truth is hidden among the paths of falsehood, the meaning of religion is unknown, its spirit has been extinguished from its expressions and methods, and nothing remains but outward forms that their inner states do not correspond to, and bodily movements that their hearts do not follow; when desires dominate, so that no longing remains to move people to action except what relates to food, drink, adornment, finery, positions and titles; when aspirations cling to false glory, and everyone loves to be praised for what he did not do; when the deficient seeks to complete what he lacks by belittling the perfect; and when, in this, the great and the small, the ruler and the ruled, the ignorant and the one titled with the title of scholar become equal. When people reach this state, the voice of truth weakens, and those who hear from among them look down on the one who calls to it, and the noble verse applies to them." End of quote.
